why: follow-redirects (resolved 2026-10-23): axios's follow-redirects@^1.16.0 range now resolves to 1.16.1, which patches GHSA-q3jh-wrc6-jgq8 and GHSA-8r9p-f939-6h3c (also trivy CVE-2026-111755/111756); the lockfile was bumped and the two entries removed. image-size is only fixable by a framework major upgrade — expo@57 + react-native@0.72 — which is a migration, not a patch. It's BUILD-TIME tooling reached through metro/expo (image-size parser DoS), not a runtime path an external caller reaches. Tracked for the framework-upgrade work; the gate fails on anything NOT listed here. postcss/decode-uri-component/@xmldom/xmldom/uuid were previously accepted here too, but are now forced to patched versions via package.json overrides (trivy findings #83-88) and removed from this list — a baselined entry that has disappeared fails the gate on purpose, so don't re-add them without re-verifying the override still resolves. node-forge (added 2026-10-02): reached only via @expo/cli and @expo/code-signing-certificates — build/publish-time tooling, not bundled runtime code. No patched release exists (1.4.0 is latest; package unmaintained) and `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade expo-updates to 0.x, which is not viable. Revisit when Expo ships a node-forge-free releases or a patched transitive dep. braces (removed 2026-10-23): GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm was withdrawn by GitHub on 2026-10-23, so npm audit no longer reports it and the gate would fail on the stale entry.
